sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ocean Vessel Freight and Wholesale Distribution of Hydraulic Cement

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-based, heavily supplemented by EU directives and Luxembourg commercial and financial statutes; unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment protection agreements in force, including with China, Hong Kong, South Korea, Russia and the United States
Luxembourg-People's Republic of China income tax treaty and related protocols
Luxembourg double taxation agreements with more than 90 jurisdictions, including France, Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, the United States and the United Kingdom
EU Treaty framework and OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance as applied through Luxembourg domestic law
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework and BEPS Multilateral Instrument adopted by Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, specifically Articles defining the Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the operational functioning of the RBE; Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade and companies register and accounting records; Law of 19 December 2020 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; CSSF AML/CFT supervision regulations; applicable FATF standards and EU AML directives transposed into Luxembourg law.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access with limited legitimate-interest access for AML/CFT regulated entities after authorization; no unrestricted public access following implementation of the ECJ ruling on public UBO register access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: None; original notarial deed lodged with the Luxembourg Business Registers; no consular legalization required for domestically executed deeds

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or trade registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the country of origin is not a Hague Convention party, full consular legalization through the competent embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or recent official extract of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or trade registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of shareholders and beneficial owner declaration certificate of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, company registry or authorized public register in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy, with Hague Apostille or consular legalization when the issuer is a public registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each shareholder, manager and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or national identity authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy verified by the Luxembourg notary at signing; foreign certified copies may require apostille or consular legalization when not produced before the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Residential proof of address for individuals, such as utility bill or bank statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, licensed bank or public authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation into French, German or Luxembourgish where necessary; no apostille required for the underlying document if the notary reviews the original at signing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate confirming payment or blocking of the minimum SARL share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution or Luxembourg notary escrow account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: None; original directly obtained from the Luxembourg bank or notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: RCS non-confusion certificate or name clearance certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers through the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional curriculum vitae and background statement for each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed manager personally, with notarial acknowledgment where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified before the Luxembourg notary; no apostille for Luxembourg execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of shareholders, managers, directors and ultimate beneficial owners against: the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners, Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) indications, CSSF supervisory instructions, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, local Luxembourg sanctions lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements. PEP screening must be performed for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, triggering enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds documentation, and senior management approval where a PEP is identified. Negative news screening and ongoing transaction monitoring shall be continued after incorporation, and records must be retained for at least five years in accordance with Luxembourg AML/CFT law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal, including the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-filing interface and e-Forum at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in Luxembourgish, French, German or another language expressed in the Latin alphabet. The legal form suffix 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL' must appear in the corporate name. Non-Latin characters, Cyrillic, Middle Eastern scripts, East Asian characters or unusual diacritics must be transliterated into a standard Latin-alphabet equivalent as approved by the notary. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name recorded in the RCS, and must not mislead the public as to the nature, nationality, size or regulated status of the company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name clearance certificate issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers is valid for 30 days and must be consumed in the notarial incorporation deed within that period. There is no standard administrative extension mechanism; if the certificate lapses, the applicant must file a new non-confusion certificate request. If the proposed name is rejected on the grounds of identical or confusing similarity to an existing RCS entry, the applicant may, within 15 days from receipt of the LBR rejection notice, submit a written challenge through the LBR e-Forum requesting reasoned reconsideration. The applicant may also instruct the Luxembourg notary to prepare an alternate name and obtain a new non-confusion certificate. Where rejection is based on a prohibited token requiring prior ministerial approval, the applicant must either obtain the required prior approval from the competent ministry/CSSF or abandon the token. A final refusal can be contested before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement, commercial chamber) by a civil motion to order registration or to compel LBR to state the grounds of refusal; refusal of ministerial authorization is separately appealable before the Administrative Tribunal within one month.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as a stand-alone registered office for a Luxembourg SARL. The statutory and administrative seat must be located in Luxembourg with a physical, serviceable address at which legal and statutory records may be inspected. A licensed professional domiciliation arrangement is permitted where a Luxembourg law firm or service provider hosts the registered office, receives mail, and makes premises available for statutory record-keeping, but a post-office box or pure mail-forwarding virtual office does not satisfy notarial and RCS practice for incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low single-digit risk for the disclosed business scope. The estimated annual probability of an unannounced Luxembourg Business Registers or FIU administrative address inspection is approximately 4-6%; an unannounced CSSF AML/CFT on-site inspection is estimated below 2% for a non-licensed portland cement wholesale and construction materials trading SARL. The probability increases to approximately 8-10% if the professional domiciliation provider is itself subject to a compliance review or adverse regulatory event.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee for share capital blocking certificate and attestation, prevailing market tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SARL with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
Publication of the incorporation notice in the electronic compendium of Luxembourg companies and associations (RESA)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of ultimate beneficial owner information in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
French or German certified translation of foreign company documents and ancillary certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Luxembourg translation provider or authorized translator

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign incorporation and good-standing documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the document country of origin and, where applicable, the Luxembourg embassy or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff and apostille fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN and EU sanctions screening for shareholders, managers and ultimate beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark subscription for pre-incorporation due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional domiciliation and registered office service for the first quarter following incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg corporate service provider or law firm

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016 modernizing company law; SARL regime at Articles 710-1 to 710-26; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 5, rue Plaetis, L-2338 Luxembourg; electronic filing via www.lbr.lu and e-justice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif) containing the articles of association (Statuts), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed capital (Article 710-1, 1915 Law as amended). Capital must be fully subscribed; each cash share must be paid to at least 25% of nominal value at subscription (EUR 3,000 minimum), while in-kind shares must be fully paid at subscription; the paid-up amount is blocked in a Luxembourg bank account (compte bloqué) or with the Caisse de Consignation until RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
1. RESOLVED, that the deed of incorporation and the articles of association of the Company are hereby adopted.
2. RESOLVED, that the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 1,000 fully subscribed shares of EUR 12 each, is confirmed as subscribed and paid.
3. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [street], L-[postcode] Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
4. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant), with sole-signature authority, and [Name] as co-signatory.
5. RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorised to open bank accounts, deposit capital, file with the RCS, and complete VAT, social security, and environmental registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name verification and registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary in coordination with the RCS name-search index via Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to run an RCS availability search on the proposed corporate name and confirm it is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registrations or protected marks; verify the registered office address (lease or letter of accommodation from the owner) is physically available in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in order of preference
Proof of identity of founding shareholders (passport or national ID)
Lease agreement or owner's accommodation letter for the registered office
Brief corporate purpose statement (wholesale distribution of hydraulic cement and Portland clinker)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file the next available preferred name; the notary may request an RCS administrative ruling on confusing similarity; alternatively, apply to the District Court of Luxembourg for a name conflict appeal within 1 month of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and shareholder approval of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the Statuts in French or German, including mandatory clauses: legal form (SARL), corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose limited to wholesale trade of cement and clinker, EUR 12,000 share capital divided into shares with or without nominal value, share subscription schedule, manager powers, and quorum/majority rules. Founding shareholders review and approve the final draft, initialling each page.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association prepared by the notary
Share subscription schedule covering 100% of the capital
Name availability confirmation from Step 1
Identity documents and, for corporate shareholders, extract from trade register
Anticipated UBO information for the statutory register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or shareholders identify a drafting defect, prepare an amending draft before execution; after execution, any typographical or clerical error is corrected by a notarial acte rectificatif filed with the RCS, with no re-execution by all shareholders required for purely clerical issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital account and deposit of paid-up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or the Caisse de Consignation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company 'en formation' with a Luxembourg bank; transfer the statutory minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 (25% of EUR 12,000), though market practice is to block the full EUR 12,000; the bank issues a blocking certificate (certificat de blocage / attestation de consignation) confirming the funds are deposited and unavailable until the RCS registration, or the funds may be consigned with the Caisse de Consignation.
required_dossiers: Account opening application for a company in formation
Draft articles of association and deed of incorporation
Passport or ID of signatories and UBOs
Source of funds declaration and bank KYC/AML questionnaire
Reference letters or corporate extracts for shareholder due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC queries or refuses the account, provide enhanced due diligence pack (bank references, audited financials of shareholders, CV and residence proof of the Gérant) or apply to an alternative Luxembourg PSP; if the Caisse de Consignation is used, ensure the consignment receipt is issued in the company-in-formation name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public attached to the Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders appear personally or by authenticated power of attorney before the notary; the notary reads the deed, verifies the bank blocking certificate and subscription schedules, and records shareholder declarations of acceptance of management functions; the deed is signed in original, with certified copies issued for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final executed share subscription schedules
Bank blocking certificate or consignment receipt
Powers of attorney for absent shareholders
Founding shareholders' identity documents and proof of legal capacity
Certified translations of foreign corporate documents, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed contains a substantive omission, the notary must convene the shareholders for an amending notarial deed before filing; if a shareholder fails to appear at the execution, adjourn and re-notarize within a reasonable period; registration deadlines remain suspended until the corrected execution is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the incorporation dossier electronically with the RCS: certified copy of the notarial deed, banking certificate, UBO declaration, and payment of the state registration fee (approximately EUR 24.75); the RCS examines the file, issues the registration number (N° RCS B…), and upon registration the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation and Statuts
Bank blocking certificate / Caisse de Consignation receipt
UBO declaration under the Law of 13 January 2019 (RBE)
RCS registration fee payment confirmation
Notary's certificate of legal compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal (e.g., incomplete annex, translation requirement), the notary corrects and resubmits within the RCS deadline; an appeal against an RCS refusal is lodged with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 40 days of notification; legal personality is retroactive to the filing date only if cured within the statutory window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and post-registration statutory clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RESA); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); STATEC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the deed is automatically published in the electronic RESA legal gazette; the company then registers for VAT (n° TVA) with the AEDT, for social security as an employer with the CCSS, and with STATEC; the natural-person manager verifies eligibility for business establishment and, if premises are used for warehousing, files the municipal establishment permit application.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (extrait du RCS)
Certified copy of the articles of association
VAT registration form (AEDT Form 101N or online eTVA application)
Employer registration declaration to CCSS
Lease agreement and proof of commercial premises
Business establishment permit questionnaire (Law of 2 September 2011)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT or social security filings attract administrative fines and interest; submit an ex-officio late-filing declaration with a mitigation request to the AEDT or CCSS; if the municipal establishment permit is contested, appeal to the communal college and thereafter to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within 3 months; the RCS extract constitutes definitive proof of legal existence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Direction de l'industrie); municipal authority of the commune of the registered office under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments; Administration de l'environnement for environmental compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific industrial license is mandated for wholesale distribution of hydraulic cement and Portland clinker. If the company operates a warehouse, silo, or transshipment point, it must obtain the general business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 and, where applicable, the municipal permit for a classified establishment (autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement classé) under the amended Law of 10 June 1999.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Administration) of the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure wholesale distribution: the activity does not meet the Annex I or Annex II thresholds of the amended Law of 15 December 2011 on environmental impact assessment; a simplified municipal 'établissement classé' notification or authorization may apply only where on-site bulk storage of cement/clinker exceeds the communal regulatory capacity thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If a cement silo or warehouse is operated: baghouse/dust filter emissions limited to a reference BAT-indicative value of no more than 20-30 mg/Nm3 for particulate matter; fugitive dust from loading/unloading suppressed by enclosed conveyors or water spraying; stormwater from paved areas contained and discharged per municipal sewer ordinance; no point-source VOC discharge for this commodity; residual waste and cement spillage handled under the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management through authorized collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) preliminary inspection and clearance for warehouse/office premises, including extinguishers, emergency egress, and signage; structural load verification of any cement silo or elevated storage by a certified engineering bureau; occupational safety: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) workplace clearance with exposure controls for cement dust (respiratory protection, ventilation), plus accident-prevention attestation; building occupancy clearance issued by the communal authority under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 and municipal building regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — the Luxembourg Registration, Estates and VAT Administration — is the competent authority for VAT registration, audit and refund matters. Direct corporate income tax is administered separately by the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); customs export formalities are administered by the Administration des douanes et accises (ADA). Official e-government portals: myguichet.lu, guichet.lu, pfi.public.lu (interactive tax platform), lbr.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 — For the resident LU SARL, execute the notarial deed of incorporation and register the company with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), obtaining the alphanumeric RCS corporate number (format B#######), which serves as the corporate identifier for direct-tax purposes at the ACD. STEP 2 — Submit the electronic VAT registration application to the AEDT through a myguichet.lu business account prior to commencing taxable supplies, attaching the articles of incorporation, RCS excerpt, manager identification and proof of effective management in Luxembourg; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by 8 digits. STEP 3 — Apply to the ADA for an EORI number to lodge customs export declarations. STEP 4 — Register for employer obligations with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) only if payroll is maintained in Luxembourg. STEP 5 — For foreign entities without a Luxembourg establishment, the same AEDT route applies without RCS registration; non-EU suppliers must appoint an approved Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative before the first taxable supply. All registrations must be completed before the first taxable event.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box or elective pass-through system. The SARL is by law an opaque resident corporation subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax. Available mechanisms: (i) group tax consolidation (fiscal unity) election under Article 164bis LIR for 95%-owned resident companies, with a 5-year irrevocable commitment; (ii) the participation exemption regime (Sections 115(5) and 166(6) LIR) for qualifying dividends and capital gains, subject to holding-period and substance conditions; (iii) the intellectual property income election under Article 50bis LIR granting an 80% income exemption for qualifying IP; (iv) hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD I/II are mandatory and not elective. The wholesale trading SARL cannot elect transparent treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), the Luxembourg value added tax implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — first-euro registration for an EU-established taxable person. Luxembourg law imposes no tax-free turnover threshold on a resident SARL engaged in wholesale supplies; VAT registration and charging obligations commence from the first taxable transaction. The domestic small-enterprise franchise under Article 57 LTVL is reserved exclusively to resident micro-traders, is subject to strict turnover ceilings and cannot be applied by a bulk export wholesaler. Non-established foreign suppliers must likewise register from the first euro unless the reverse-charge, distance-sale or warehousing carve-outs apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance regime, no continuous transaction controls (CTC), no state-operated e-invoicing API and no digital fiscal stamping ('cachet fiscal') currently applies to domestic or cross-border B2B trade in Luxembourg. Structured e-invoicing is mandatory only for B2G transactions, where invoices must comply with EN 16931/Peppol BIS when supplied to Luxembourg public entities. Export invoices for bulk clinker may be issued in paper or electronic form, provided that authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility are preserved, and the invoice must show the statutory export zero-rating reference. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing will apply in Luxembourg only after transposition, with no obligation before the 2030s.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Bulk supplies of Portland cement clinker qualify for the export zero-rating of Article 54 LTVL (implementing Article 146(1)(a) VAT Directive) where the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union to a third-country destination by the supplier, the non-EU purchaser or a third party on their behalf, and leave the EU within the statutory 90-day dispatch window from the date of supply. The SARL bears the burden of proof and must hold an accepted customs export declaration together with complete transport and banking evidence before the zero rate may be applied. The exemption extends to exports leaving via another EU port of exit (e.g., Rotterdam, Antwerp or Dunkirk) provided the Luxembourg seller is named in the export documentation and the welfare transport to the non-EU destination is continuous and substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/EXS) lodged in the EU Customs Decisions System and cleared by the customs office of exit
Ocean Bill of Lading (shipped-on-board) evidencing carriage of the clinker cargo to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing collection of the export consideration in alignment with the invoice value
Commercial invoice with full seller/buyer identification, Incoterms (FOB/CIF/FCA basis), bulk quantity and the export zero-rating reference
Packing list and weight certificate / draft survey report for the vessel-loaded clinker cargo
Transport contract, charter party or booking confirmation together with vessel call certificate at the EU port of exit
Freight and cargo insurance certificates where CIF or CIP terms of sale have been agreed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT subjects export zero-rating claims to three-way document matching among the customs exit record, the ocean Bill of Lading and the banking receipt. Where the export movement, the consignee identity or the inward foreign-exchange repatriation cannot be substantiated, the AEDT retroactively recharacterises the supply as taxable, assesses Luxembourg VAT at 17%, denies or claws back input VAT on the goods and freight, and adds statutory late-payment interest. Administrative penalties are graduated from 10% up to 100% of the evaded tax, and intent-based concealment doubles the maximum. Deliberate submission of false export declarations, forged bills of lading or fabricated remittance certificates exposes the SARL and its managers to criminal tax and customs fraud prosecution — fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment — and extends the reassessment window from the ordinary five years to ten years. AEO status moderates inspection frequency but does not attenuate clawback liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating inside the Eurosystem; the European Central Bank and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance set monetary and external-payments policy. Luxembourg does not have a separate exchange-control authority; capital movement rules derive from EU Treaty Articles 63 to 65.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully convertible on both current and capital account. No Luxembourg registration, licensing, or approval is required for cross-border capital movement or profit remittance. Dividends and retained profits can be converted into any market currency and remitted, subject only to Luxembourg withholding taxes and the standard Anti-Money-Laundering/CRS information obligations of the paying institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, compulsory conversion, or repatriation timeline applies to export earnings. A Luxembourg wholesale trader may lawfully hold exported proceeds in foreign-currency accounts with an authorised Luxembourg/European Economic Area bank, fund onward working-capital disbursements, or hedge; there is no deadline or percentage requirement. Only standard transaction reporting for AML/CTF and CSSF statistical purposes is mandatory.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate. An EEA-authorised EMI/Payment Institution exercising a Luxembourg passport can open payment accounts and execute SEPA/SWIFT transfers, and may provide a useful high-velocity disbursement overlay for freight payments and minor operational expenses. It is not suitable for large equity injections, trade-finance instruments, or documentary letters of credit. Non-EEA offshore EMIs cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to a Luxembourg client without a Luxembourg/EEA branch or agent under PSD2 and the Luxembourg AML/CTF law; their practical viability is Low unless licensed in Luxembourg and subject to CSSF prudential supervision.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory KYC requires reliable independent identification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners. Physical appearance is not mandated by law if the institution can perform eIDAS-compliant remote electronic identification, but in practice many tier-1 Luxembourg banks insist on one physical or notarised meeting for directors/UBOs, especially when shareholding is non-EU. Remote opening can be available where a Luxembourg credit institution or lawyer conducts due diligence; alternatively, the SARL may appoint a local authorised signatory while the UBO still submits notarised identity, source of wealth, and bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value bulk cement clinker shipments and cargo invoices inconsistent with modest registered capital and office footprint; transaction-profile red flag for trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed supply and distribution contracts, vessel charter parties or bill-of-lading, storage warehouse agreements, customs declarations, annual audited/CFO-prepared financial projections, packing lists, quality/shipping certificates, and the corporate treasury policy showing clear payment flows and counterparty credit approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU or zero/low-tax jurisdiction shareholders in the Luxembourg SARL ownership chain; beneficial-ownership transparency concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Luxembourg RBE (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract, notarised group structure chart, tax residence certificates and board profiles of all UBOs, bank reference from the home relationship bank, source-of-funds documentation for the capital subscription, and parental audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound capital injections or trade settlements from entities with no historic KYC; high velocity and cross-border payment corridors to cement-manufacturing jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an annual cash-flow model, signed and dated board resolution approving each payment corridor, invoice and LC drafts, counterparty onboarding file (company extract, beneficial-owner identification, sanctions screening), and a written negative-news explanation for each trading partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained third-party payments or pivoting from wholesale trading into lending/treasury activities outside the SARL's corporate objects.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amend and notarise articles of association, maintain a separate operations account, produce board minutes specifying commercial purpose, ensure instruments are MiFID/EMIR compliant, and document that no unlicensed credit activity has occurred; record contract, invoice, and receipt for each operation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital/equity funding must be routed by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer where the remitter is in SEPA) to the SARL's Luxembourg bank account in the corporate legal name. Payment reference must state 'Shareholder equity contribution / capital increase' and, where required by the receiving bank, include the Luxembourg balance-of-payments category for direct-investment equity. The bank posts the credit after standard KYC/CDD and sanctions verification; back-up file includes board resolution, notarised capital increase deed, subscribed shares, and proof of source of funds. There is no central-bank filing or approval for convertible capital, but anti-money-laundering declarations apply above statutory thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for open-account telegraphic transfers to suppliers and freight providers; include full beneficiary name/IBAN/BIC, invoice/contract number, and Incoterms. For large vessel/portland clinker deliveries, use an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit opened under UCP600; the issuing bank sends an MT700, confirming bank negotiates the draft against shipping warranty/documents, and payment is executed by MT202 cover/MT103 as usual. All disbursements should pass only through cleared CRS/CSSF-regulated banking counterparties; crypto assets or unlicensed payment aggregators are excluded for treasury liquidity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards for EUR/USD, EUR/TRY and EUR/CNH, with ISDA 1998 FX Definitions and bilateral CSA/credit support.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted/inaccessible currencies where physical settlement is impractical; lawful as OTC derivatives subject to EMIR trade reporting and margin rules.
FX swaps for near-term liquidity management.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) aligning USD trade receivables/payables with EUR funding; permitted under MiFID II if the SARL obtains professional-investor treatment or receives investment advice from the clearing bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) confirming RCS data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual anniversary date of the RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing warnings and monetary penalty of EUR 20 per day; persistent non-filing may lead to forced dissolution by the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) filed and published
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Recueil électronique des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance sheet date; for fiscal year ending 31 December, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order to produce accounts, late filing penalty up to EUR 10,000; criminal sanctions for directors for non-disclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (form 100) and municipal business tax return (form 101) combined
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg direct tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies, by 31 December of the following tax year; for non-calendar year, within six months after accounting year-end, extended to 31 December if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate tax assessment based on estimate, late payment interest at 0.6% per month; fines up to EUR 25,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (form 102) including minimum net wealth tax calculation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg direct tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as income tax return: 31 December of the following tax year for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest at 0.6% per month; administrative fines and loss of tax advantages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (convalidation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS, Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual anniversary of the initial UBO registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalty up to EUR 125,000 and/or six months imprisonment; administrative fine up to EUR 5,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must undergo a statutory audit if it exceeds at least two of the following limits for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50. Audit is also compulsory for public-interest entities, credit institutions, insurance undertakings, and companies whose securities are admitted to trading.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the law of 19 December 2002; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts and for certain unlisted companies under EU rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Once a year, the SARL must confirm the accuracy of UBO information in the RCS beneficial owner register; changes must be filed within 30 days of the underlying change. The annual confirmation is performed electronically in the LBR UBO module and must be completed before the anniversary of the registration. Failure triggers criminal penalties and may impede distributions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typical annual fee range in Luxembourg for a registered office/domiciliation agent: USD 1,400 – 3,000, exclusive of VAT; higher for enhanced AML/KYC duties.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For a wholesale distribution SARL meeting audit thresholds: estimated USD 8,500 – 18,000 for a first-year audit, lower for annual repeat; small companies under thresholds: USD 2,000 – 6,000 for voluntary review.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% in Luxembourg City (17.00% corporate income tax + 7.00% solidarity surcharge on the corporate income tax + 6.75% municipal business tax; municipal business tax rate varies by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for SARLs. Applicable preferential measures: 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual property income under the IP box, full participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, and accelerated depreciation for qualifying operating assets. The aggregate effective CIT rate may be materially below 24.94% for such exempt or preferentially taxed income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 470 (combined declaration for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax) filed with the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD); mandatory electronic filing through myGuichet.lu using a LuxTrust-certified digital certificate and the ACD e-file space.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Separate monthly and quarterly filings exist for VAT, wage withholding tax, and social security declarations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return is due by 31 May of the following calendar year. For non-calendar fiscal years, the return is due by the last day of the fifth month following the fiscal year-end. The ACD routinely extends the deadline to 31 December for taxpayers filing electronically and providing the required cooperation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg RCS registration number, matricule fiscal, legal form, ISIC/NACE class, office address, and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LU SARL is the taxpayer. Foreign shareholders must not be listed as co-filers; a non-resident parent is relevant only in the attachment identifying direct and indirect participations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Net profit per commercial accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Starting point of the tax reconciliation: profit or loss per audited statutory accounts prepared in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenues from bulk transshipment, ocean freight margins, and wholesale sales of Portland cement clinker must be included. Foreign back-office service allocations must be supported by valid contracts and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible corporate income tax and municipal business tax, fines, excessive director fees, non-arm's-length interest, deemed royalties, and 7% solidarity surcharge type expenses not deductible under Luxembourg law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to a foreign shareholder in the form of management fees or commissions which lack economic substance must be added back unless the beneficiary proves the fee is arm's-length and beneficial ownership exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Municipal business tax base adjustment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the taxable basis for the communal trade tax, including add-backs for long-term interest and rental payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident shareholder is generally added back for municipal business tax purposes; treaty relief on the CIT portion does not automatically apply to the municipal business tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Participation exemption and IP box
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of exempt dividend income and capital gains on qualifying participations and of qualifying IP income deductible at an 80% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach legal ownership documents, corporate income tax residence certificates of investee entities, and a signed statement confirming the 12-month holding period for the participation exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year deduction of tax losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the original tax year of each loss tranche. Luxembourg permits losses to be carried forward for 17 years; a change in shareholder composition may trigger an anti-abuse review when the principal activity of the SARL is changed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of intra-group transactions including purchases, sales, interest, royalties, management fees, freight income, and intercompany balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party bulk cement clinker sales and LC/TT payment flows must be reported. Attach the transfer pricing dossier when the thresholds for Master File or Local File are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net wealth assessed on total Luxembourg and foreign fixed assets less eligible liabilities, at the ordinary net wealth tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-dominated SARL, assets must be allocated to the Luxembourg balance sheet; bank accounts and trade receivables associated with the clinker trading activity remain taxable unless exempted by law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers taxation d'office by the ACD, a 10% mise en recouvrement surcharge on assessed tax, monthly late-payment interest on unpaid tax, and additional fines for failure to file attachments. Deliberate understatement can attract administrative penalties up to 100% of the additional tax, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000, and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends distributed by the SARL to non-resident shareholders. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive provides a 0% source rate when a qualifying EU parent holds at least 10% for at least 12 uninterrupted months; many comprehensive double tax treaties reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner and provide an authentic residence certificate (TRC) issued by its tax authority, together with legal ownership confirmation. At the payment date the Luxembourg SARL may apply the treaty/PSD rate if all forms are on file and valid; otherwise 15% must be withheld and the shareholder must file a refund reclaim with the ACD within the statutory limitation period. The ACD also requires a certificate of good standing for the distributing SARL and a declaration of non-existence of a permanent establishment of the shareholder in Luxembourg.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by the SARL to non-resident lenders is generally exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax when lent at arm's length in the ordinary course of business. Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to a 10% domestic withholding tax; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may grant 0% relief for royalty payments to an associated EU resident company, and double tax treaties typically reduce the royalty rate to 0-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File threshold: annual related-party transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 for any category of goods, services, royalties, financing, or freight-related intercompany charges. Master File/CbCR threshold: worldwide consolidated group revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more. The ACD may request transfer pricing documentation even below these thresholds when the intra-group price or margin appears abnormal.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations in the BVI/Cayman sense, but domestic jurisprudence, Art. 56 LIR, and ACD Circular 56/1 require functional, asset, and risk substance aligned with reported intercompany compensation. For an ocean-vessel freight and wholesale cement clinker SARL, the company must demonstrate local commercial negotiation, physical movement monitoring, invoice management, and business risk assumption through employees, offices, board minutes, and payment records. Letterbox companies that merely pass invoices and arrange LC/TT funds without active decision-making are vulnerable to tax recharacterization, treaty abuse denial, and criminal audit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting taxable revenue from ocean vessel freight and bulk cement clinker sales, forging bills of lading, backdating invoices, destroying accounting records, or filing false CIT returns with the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties: imprisonment up to five years and fine up to EUR 250,000; civil reassessment of full tax, 10-100% administrative penalties, monthly late-payment interest, and disclosure of the debt in public registers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authorize false returns are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties, and interest. Luxembourg courts may impose travel bans, freezing orders, disqualification from directorship, and personal bankruptcy where assets were moved abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling Portland cement clinker to a related foreign trading vehicle at an artificially low price, or paying freight commissions to a related non-resident entity without actual vessel chartering or cargo management substance, while failing to prepare the Local File despite exceeding EUR 100,000 in related-party flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD recharacterization of income under Art. 56 LIR, upward adjustment of SARL taxable income, denial of expenses, imposition of a 10% filing penalty and up to 100% understatement penalty, plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to ACD recovery actions when the transfer pricing file is absent or fraudulent; repeated violations trigger director disqualification and criminal liability for aiding tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL has no employees, no office, no local booking notes, no board meetings, and no commercial risk management for clinker cargoes; it simply issues invoices and receives LC/TT payments on behalf of a foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Refusal of tax residence and treaty benefits under Circular 56/1; reallocation of profits to the foreign parent; administrative fines for false declarations; potential judicial liquidation and strike-off from the Luxembourg trade register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners can be liable for unpaid taxes, prohibited from managing Luxembourg entities, and subject to extradition assistance in EU cross-border tax investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of Swift LC or TT payment rails to finance fictitious or double-invoiced cement clinker shipments, concealed cargo rerouting, false commodity invoices, omission of beneficial owner information, or transactions with shell suppliers located in high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accessory money laundering penalties under the Luxembourg AML regime: fines up to EUR 1.25-5 million, asset freezing, confiscation of cargo proceeds, professional bans, and criminal prosecution of the Luxembourg responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal conviction, imprisonment, personal asset seizure, and travel restrictions when they deliberately process fraudulent trade documents through the Luxembourg entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Dividend Repatriation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to a non-resident shareholder as a disguised dividend through consultancy fees, excessive charter-party payments, or interest charged to the SARL without withholding the statutory 15% or documenting treaty exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification as constructive dividend, recapture of 15% withholding tax, late payment interest, up to 10% late-filing penalty, denial of expense deduction, and liability for solidarity surcharge and municipal tax adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL is the withholding agent; directors are jointly liable for the uncollected withholding tax and may be personally pursued where the entity is insolvent. Serious concealment can lead to criminal tax fraud charges.
